3: # TiffCraft
4: 
5: TiffCraft is a header-only C++20 library for reading uncompressed TIFF images.
6: It provides a customizable image-data export interface and requires no separate
7: library binary.
8: 
9: # Objectives
10: 
11: TiffCraft is designed based on the following principles:
12: 
13: - Permissive license: to be used in open source and proprietary software.
14: - C++ header-only: to easy integration onto existing projects.
15: - Flexible but simple API: for ease of use.
16: - Feature complete: to cover a wide variety of use cases.
17:   - TiffCraft is NOT feature complete at this time! The objective is for guiding
18:     on-going development.
19: 
20: # Usage
21: 
22: For quick access to TIFF image pixel data with individual pixels aligned to
23: word boundaries (i.e. 8 bits, 16 bits, or 32 bits), you could use code like
24: the following:
25: 
26: ```C++
27: #include <tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp>
28: #include <functional>
29: 
30: int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
31:   if (argc < 2) { return 1; }
32:   TiffCraft::TiffExporterAny tiffExporter;
33:   TiffCraft::load(argv[1], std::ref(tiffExporter));
34:   auto image = tiffExporter.takeImage();
35: 
36:   // your own image processing code
37: 
38:   return 0;
39: }
40: ```
41: 
42: TiffExporterAny will decode and convert pixels to a flat-buffer (i.e.
43:  `std::vector<std::byte>`) with 1, 2, or 4 bytes per sample the source pixel
44: format. For example, an image with 2-bits per sample is exported as an 8-bit
45: image.
46: 
47: TiffCraft is header-only and can be consumed by copying the headers into
48: your project. No build step required: no compiled artifact, no link step, and
49: no CMake needed (CMake-based consumption is documented separately).
50: 
51: # Which headers do you need?
52: 
53: TiffCraft is header-only; copy the headers from `include/tiffcraft/` into
54: your project and include them directly. No CMake required (CMake-based
55: consumption is documented separately).
56: 
57: When copying the headers, keep them together in one directory; if the folder
58: is renamed, update the consumer-facing `#include <tiffcraft/...>` paths in
59: your own code accordingly.
60: 
61: - `TiffImage.hpp`: core TIFF reading; self-contained.
62: - `TiffExporter.hpp`: flat-buffer pixel decoding; requires `TiffImage.hpp`.
63: - `TiffStdOut.hpp`: metadata output/printing; requires `TiffImage.hpp`.
64: - `TiffCraft.hpp`: umbrella header; includes everything.
65: 
66: `TiffImage.hpp` is self-contained; the other headers depend on it by filename
67: (e.g. `#include "TiffImage.hpp"`), which resolves relative to the including
68: header's own directory, so they can live together in any folder. The
69: `tiffcraft/` folder name applies only to consumer-facing include paths (e.g.
70: `#include <tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp>`), which are in the user's own code and
71: must be updated if the folder is renamed.
72: 
73: # Advanced usage
74: 
75: Users that prefer to decode and handle the image pixel data themselves, or need
76: to handle multiple frames per image, could write their own handler:
77: 
78: ```C++
79: #include <tiffcraft/TiffImage.hpp>
80: #include <iostream>
81: 
82: int main() {
83:   TiffCraft::load("image.tiff",
84:     [](const TiffCraft::TiffImage::Header& header,
85:         const TiffCraft::TiffImage::IFD& ifd,
86:         TiffCraft::TiffImage::ImageData imageData) {
87:       std::cout << "Loaded IFD with " << ifd.entries().size()
88:                 << " entries." << std::endl;
89:       std::cout << "Image data size: " << imageData.size() << std::endl;
90: 
91:       // Add your own image processing code here
92: 
93:     });
94: 
95:   return 0;
96: }
97: ```
98: 
99: # Printing image metadata
100: 
101: Include `TiffStdOut.hpp` to print TIFF metadata and IFD entries with the
102: standard library streams:
103: 
104: ```C++
105: #include <tiffcraft/TiffStdOut.hpp>
106: #include <iostream>
107: 
108: int main() {
109:   TiffCraft::load("image.tiff",
110:     [](const TiffCraft::TiffImage::Header& header,
111:         const TiffCraft::TiffImage::IFD& ifd,
112:         TiffCraft::TiffImage::ImageData imageData) {
113:       std::cout << header << "\n";
114:       std::cout << ifd << "\n";
115:     });
116: 
117:   return 0;
118: }
119: ```
120: 
121: `toString(Tag)` and `toString(Type)` are also available as standalone helpers;
122: stream operators exist for `Header`, `Entry`, `IFD`, and `TiffImage`.
123: 
124: # Features
125: 
126: TiffCraft supports the following features:
127: 
128: - Reading TIFF images
129:   - Read and display image metadata
130:   - Bilevel, grayscale, palette-color, and RGB images
131:     - Varying number of bits per sample
132:     - RGB images are supported only for 3-channel images (no extra samples)
133: - Compression is NOT supported yet.
134: - Writing TIFF images is NOT supported yet.
135: 
136: Advanced users could use TiffCraft for other configurations than those
137: enumerated above by writing their customizing any of the existing exporter
138: classes, or writing their own from scratch.
139: 
140: # CMake consumption
141: 
142: ## FetchContent
143: 
144: TiffCraft is header-only and can be consumed directly from its git
145: repository with CMake's `FetchContent` module:
146: 
147: ```cmake
148: include(FetchContent)
149: 
150: FetchContent_Declare(
151:   TiffCraft
152:   GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/danielm5/tiffcraft.git
153:   GIT_TAG <release tag>   # e.g. the latest release tag
154: )
155: FetchContent_MakeAvailable(TiffCraft)
156: 
157: target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE TiffCraft::TiffCraft)
158: ```
159: 
160: When consumed this way, the `TIFFCRAFT_BUILD_ALL` option defaults to `OFF`,
161: so the library's tests, apps, and examples are not built. The same applies
162: when consuming via `add_subdirectory` from a local checkout.
163: 
164: ## find_package
165: 
166: To consume a CMake-installed TiffCraft package:
167: 
168: ```sh
169: cmake --install /path/to/tiffcraft/build/gcc-linux-release --prefix /path/to/install
170: ```
171: 
172: ```cmake
173: find_package(TiffCraft REQUIRED)
174: 
175: target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE TiffCraft::TiffCraft)
176: ```
177: 
178: The installed package provides the `TiffCraft::TiffCraft` namespaced target and
179: the public headers under `include/tiffcraft`.
180: 
181: # Feedback
182:

184: [GitHub issue](https://github.com/danielm5/tiffcraft/issues/new/choose)
185: if you have suggestions, feature requests, or bug reports.
186:

1: # YCbCr (PhotometricInterpretation = 6) Support Reference
2: 
3: This document describes YCbCr (`PhotometricInterpretation = 6`) images as
4: defined by Section 21 of the TIFF 6.0 specification.
5: 
6: ## Scope
7: 
8: - YCbCr image encoding as defined by TIFF 6.0 Section 21.
9: - Conversion between RGB and YCbCr.
10: - Chroma subsampling, positioning, and reference black/white handling.
11: - Minimum requirements for a valid YCbCr TIFF.
12: - Mapping of the test images in `tests/ycbcr_images/` to the specification
13:   topics they exercise.
14: 
15: ## Tag definitions
16: 
17: The following TIFF tags describe the color information of an image whose
18: `PhotometricInterpretation = 6` (YCbCr). They are defined in TIFF 6.0
19: Section 21.
20: 
21: | Tag | Name | TIFF value | Type | Count | Default | Description |
22: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
23: | 529 | YCbCrCoefficients | 0x0211 | RATIONAL (5) / SRATIONAL (10) | 3 | ITU-R BT.601 luma coefficients | Coefficients used for the transformation from RGB to YCbCr. |
24: | 530 | YCbCrSubsampling | 0x0212 | SHORT (3) | 2 | 2, 2 | Horizontal and vertical subsampling factors of the chroma components. |
25: | 531 | YCbCrPositioning | 0x0213 | SHORT (3) | 1 | 1 | Positioning of the chroma samples relative to the luminance samples. |
26: | 532 | ReferenceBlackWhite | 0x0214 | RATIONAL (5) | 6 | (0, 255, 128, 255, 128, 255) | Reference black and white data values (headroom/footroom) per component. |
27: 
28: Notes on the individual tags:
29: 
30: - **YCbCrCoefficients (529 / 0x0211):** Type RATIONAL (TIFF data type 5) or
31:   SRATIONAL (TIFF data type 10), with **3 values** (the RGB -> YCbCr
32:   transformation coefficients, e.g. the luma row). Defaults to the ITU-R BT.601
33:   coefficients (approximately 0.299, 0.587, 0.114 for the red, green and blue
34:   contributions to luma).
35: - **YCbCrSubsampling (530 / 0x0212):** Type SHORT (TIFF data type 3), **2
36:   values** — the horizontal subsampling factor and the vertical subsampling
37:   factor. Default is **2, 2** (chroma subsampled by 2 on both axes). Legal
38:   factors are **1, 2 and 4**
39:   (1 = no subsampling, 2 = half resolution, 4 = quarter resolution along the
40:   axis).
41: - **YCbCrPositioning (531 / 0x0213):** Type SHORT (TIFF data type 3), **1
42:   value**. Default is **1 = centered**. The alternative value is **2 = co-sited**
43:   (chroma sample points aligned with luma sample positions, as used e.g. in
44:   broadcast 4:2:2 workflows).
45: - **ReferenceBlackWhite (532 / 0x0214):** Type RATIONAL (TIFF data type 5), **6
46:   values**. The values are grouped in pairs of (reference black, reference
47:   white) per pixel component, ordered like the components of the
48:   `PhotometricInterpretation = 6` image (Y, Cb, Cr). Default value set:
49:   Y black/white = 0/255, Cb black/white = 128/255, Cr black/white = 128/255.
50: 
51: ## Conversion formulas
52: 
53: ### Generalized RGB <-> YCbCr
54: 
55: The conversion is parameterized by the luma coefficients `Lr`, `Lg` and `Lb`
56: from `YCbCrCoefficients` (tag 529), which satisfy `Lr + Lg + Lb = 1`. Two
57: helper constants give the chroma scale factors:
58: 
59: - `Lr' = 2 * (1 - Lr)`
60: - `Lb' = 2 * (1 - Lb)`
61: 
62: All `Y`, `Cb` and `Cr` values below are **full-range** values obtained from
63: the stored codes by the `ReferenceBlackWhite` scaling described later. The
64: forward relations are:
65: 
66: - `Y = Lr*R + Lg*G + Lb*B`
67: - `Cb_full = (B - Y) / Lb'`
68: - `Cr_full = (R - Y) / Lr'`
69: 
70: They produce zero chroma at neutral; the chroma neutral offset (128 for
71: 8-bit samples) is added when the codes are stored.
72: 
73: The inverse follows by substituting the red and blue relations into
74: `G = (Y - Lr*R - Lb*B) / Lg` and simplifying with `Lg = 1 - Lr - Lb`:
75: 
76: ```text
77: R = Y + Cr_full * Lr'
78: B = Y + Cb_full * Lb'
79: G = (Y - Lr*(Y + Cr_full*Lr') - Lb*(Y + Cb_full*Lb')) / Lg
80:   = Y - (Lb*Lb'/Lg)*Cb_full - (Lr*Lr'/Lg)*Cr_full
81: ```
82: 
83: **Default coefficients (ITU-R BT.601, the default for tag 529):** `Lr =
84: 0.299`, `Lg = 0.587`, `Lb = 0.114`. Then `Lr' = 1.402`, `Lb' = 1.772`,
85: `Lr*Lr'/Lg ≈ 0.714136` and `Lb*Lb'/Lg ≈ 0.344136`, giving the familiar
86: 
87: - `R = Y + 1.402*Cr_full`
88: - `B = Y + 1.772*Cb_full`
89: - `G = Y - 0.344136*Cb_full - 0.714136*Cr_full`
90: 
91: Under the default reference values the neutral chroma code 128 maps to a
92: full-range value of zero, so `Cb_full = Cb_code - 128` and `Cr_full =
93: Cr_code - 128`; the traditional `R = Y + 1.402 * (Cr - 128)` is exactly
94: this default-coefficient case written with stored codes.
95: 
96: ### Reference black/white / headroom and footroom
97: 
98: The `ReferenceBlackWhite` tag supplies, per component, a reference black value
99: and a reference white value. These define the headroom/footroom range of the
100: image data: the black value corresponds to the black end of the coding range and
101: the white value to the white end. The values stored in the image are **codes**;
102: `ReferenceBlackWhite` defines how those codes scale into full-range values when
103: converting to RGB.
104: 
105: For each component the forward scaling is:
106: 
107: `FullRangeValue = (code - ReferenceBlack) * CodingRange / (ReferenceWhite - ReferenceBlack)`
108: 
109: and the reverse scaling is:
110: 
111: `code = (FullRangeValue * (ReferenceWhite - ReferenceBlack) / CodingRange) + ReferenceBlack`
112: 
113: `CodingRange` is the range of full-range values: `2^BitsPerSample - 1` for Y and
114: RGB (255 for 8-bit samples), but **127 for Cb and Cr**. That difference matters:
115: with the default reference values Cb/Cr run from code 128 to code 255, so the
116: chroma scaling reduces to `(code - 128) * 127 / (255 - 128) = code - 128`. In
117: other words `Cb_full = Cb_code - 128` and `Cr_full = Cr_code - 128` under the
118: defaults. The generalized formulas above consume these full-range values, so
119: the traditional `R = Y + 1.402 * (Cr - 128)` is exactly the default-coefficient
120: case (`Lr = 0.299`, hence `Lr' = 1.402`): the `128` is the Cb/Cr
121: `ReferenceBlack` code in that special case, not a magic number.
122: 
123: For YCbCr the default reference values are black = 0 and white = 255 for the
124: luma component (Y), and black = 128 and white = 255 for the chroma components
125: (Cb/Cr). Merely subtracting 128 is correct only for these defaults. Images with
126: headroom/footroom carry other reference values: for example, with
127: `ReferenceBlackWhite = [15, 235, 128, 240, 128, 240]` a luma code of 235 maps to
128: `255` and a luma code of 15 maps to `0`, using
129: `(code - 15) * 255 / (235 - 15)`. The chroma white reference is 240 rather than
130: the default 255, so subtracting 128 alone leaves chroma under-scaled. Readers
131: must apply the tag's scaling instead of assuming the defaults.
132: 
133: The TIFF 6.0 specification says the default `ReferenceBlackWhite` values are
134: inappropriate for Class Y images and that the tag must be supplied explicitly.
135: In practice many images omit it, so readers must fall back to the YCbCr-specific
136: defaults above (Y 0/255, Cb/Cr 128/255).
137: 
138: ## Subsampling
139: 
140: - The `YCbCrSubsampling` factors describe how the chroma components are
141:   subsampled relative to the luma component.
142: - Legal subsampling factors are **1, 2 and 4**.
143: - The chroma image dimensions are computed by rounding **up** (ceiling) the
144:   luma dimensions divided by the subsampling factor, so that no chroma sample is
145:   dropped for images whose dimensions are not evenly divisible.
146: - For images using subsampling, strip organization (`RowsPerStrip`) must be
147:   consistent with the luma/chroma grid; `RowsPerStrip` is expressed in luma
148:   rows.
149: 
150: ## Positioning
151: 
152: - `YCbCrPositioning = 1` (default): **centered** positioning of the chroma
153:   samples with respect to the luminance samples.
154: - `YCbCrPositioning = 2`: **co-sited** positioning (chroma sample points aligned
155:   with luma sample points, e.g. recommended for 4:2:2 workflows).
156: 
157: ## Minimum requirements for YCbCr images
158: 
159: In addition to the general Baseline TIFF requirements, a YCbCr file must have:
160: 
161: - `SamplesPerPixel = 3` (Y, Cb, Cr).
162: - `BitsPerSample = 8, 8, 8`.
163: - `Compression = 1` (none), `5` (LZW) or `7` (JPEG; TIFF Technical Note 2).
164: - `PhotometricInterpretation = 6` (YCbCr).
165: - `PlanarConfig = 1` (chunky) or `2` (separate).
166: - `ReferenceBlackWhite`: required by the TIFF 6.0 specification. Readers must
167:   nevertheless handle its absence by falling back to the YCbCr-specific
168:   defaults above (Y 0/255, Cb/Cr 128/255), because many real-world files omit
169:   tag 532.
170: 
171: ## Generating the test images
172: 
173: `tests/ycbcr_images/generate_ycbcr.py` recreates the fixture set. It requires
174: Python 3 and the libtiff and netpbm command-line tools (`pnmtotiff`,
175: `rgb2ycbcr`, `tiffset`, `tiffcp`, `tiff2rgba`, `tifftopnm`). From the repository
176: root, run:
177: 
178: ```sh
179: python3 tests/ycbcr_images/generate_ycbcr.py
180: ```
181: 
182: The pipeline for each fixture is:
183: 
184: 1. Write a deterministic binary P6 source PPM in pure Python (standard-library
185:    `bytes` and `zlib.crc32`; no external imaging library).
186: 2. `pnmtotiff < src.ppm > src.tif` creates an RGB TIFF.
187: 3. `rgb2ycbcr -c none -h H -v V -r HEIGHT src.tif out.tif` writes the YCbCr
188:    image. This writes all four YCbCr tags (529, 530, 531, 532) with the BT.601
189:    coefficients, centered positioning and default reference values.
190: 4. Attributes that `rgb2ycbcr` cannot produce directly are applied with
191:    `tiffset`. RATIONAL tags are set without a count, e.g.
192:    `tiffset -s YCbCrCoefficients 0.2126 0.7152 0.0722 file`. Tiled organization
193:    uses `tiffcp -t -w 16 -l 16 -c none`; because `tiffcp` refuses subsampled
194:    input it tiles a 1x1 image and the four YCbCr tags plus
195:    `PhotometricInterpretation` are restored afterwards. Separate-plane coverage
196:    for `ycbcr-planar-1x1.tif` uses `tiffcp -p separate` followed by restoring
197:    `PhotometricInterpretation` and the four YCbCr tags with `tiffset`, giving
198:    real separate-plane data. `ycbcr-planar-2x2.tif` is written by a pure-Python
199:    `struct`-based TIFF writer that gives each of the three plane segments its
200:    own strip, with consistent strip offset and byte-count arrays.
201: 5. `tiff2rgba -n -c none <tif> <rgba.tif>` followed by
202:    `tifftopnm <rgba.tif> > ycbcr-*.ppm` produces each ground-truth P6 PPM.
203: 6. Every emitted TIFF is checked by the generator's `validate_fixture`
204:    routine: it parses the IFD with `struct`, verifies the YCbCr tags and
205:    values, checks the strip/tile array lengths against the image geometry
206:    (catching inconsistent planar strip arrays), and rejects any `tiffinfo`
207:    warning or error.
208: 
209: The 18 fixtures are described in the matrix below. Of the six variant fixtures,
210: four are tag-reading tests only: `tiffset` changes tag values without
211: reorganizing pixel data. The two planar fixtures are conversion tests with
212: genuinely separate planes. The tiled fixture is additionally limited in that
213: its pixel data is **not** subsampled — the `YCbCrSubsampling` tag is set to
214: `2 2` after tiling — so it is not usable for conversion verification.
215: 
216: ## Test image matrix
217: 
218: All files are in `tests/ycbcr_images/`. The "Kind" column marks a fixture as a
219: **conversion** test (tags and pixel data agree) or a **tag-reading** test.
220: 
221: ### Subsampling fixtures
222: 
223: Nine 64x48 images with default BT.601 coefficients, centered positioning,
224: default reference values, 8-bit contiguous planes and no compression. Each
225: carries a real `YCbCrSubsampling` value written by `rgb2ycbcr`.
226: 
227: | Test image | Subsampling | Kind | Validates |
228: |---|---|---|---|
229: | `ycbcr-1x1.tif` | 1x1 | conversion | Full-resolution YCbCr with all four tags at their defaults; stripped organization. |
230: | `ycbcr-2x1.tif` | 2x1 | conversion | Horizontal-only chroma subsampling. |
231: | `ycbcr-1x2.tif` | 1x2 | conversion | Vertical-only chroma subsampling. |
232: | `ycbcr-2x2.tif` | 2x2 | conversion | Half-resolution chroma on both axes. |
233: | `ycbcr-4x1.tif` | 4x1 | conversion | Quarter-resolution horizontal chroma. |
234: | `ycbcr-1x4.tif` | 1x4 | conversion | Quarter-resolution vertical chroma. |
235: | `ycbcr-4x2.tif` | 4x2 | conversion | Mixed 4x2 chroma grid. |
236: | `ycbcr-2x4.tif` | 2x4 | conversion | Mixed 2x4 chroma grid. |
237: | `ycbcr-4x4.tif` | 4x4 | conversion | Quarter-resolution chroma on both axes. |
238: 
239: ### Variant fixtures
240: 
241: Six 64x48 images with one non-default attribute each. Of these, four are
242: tag-reading tests: `tiffset` changes the tag without reorganizing pixel data.
243: The two planar fixtures instead hold genuine separate planes.
244: 
245: | Test image | Attribute | Kind | Validates |
246: |---|---|---|---|
247: | `ycbcr-cosited.tif` | Positioning = 2 (co-sited) on a 2x2 base | tag-reading | Co-sited chroma positioning. |
248: | `ycbcr-custom-coeffs.tif` | Coefficients = 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722 on a 1x1 base | tag-reading | Non-default luma coefficients (tag 529). |
249: | `ycbcr-custom-refbw.tif` | RefBW = 15/235/128/240/128/240 on a 1x1 base | tag-reading | Headroom/footroom reference values (tag 532). |
250: | `ycbcr-planar-1x1.tif` | PlanarConfig = 2, separate planes on a 1x1 base | conversion | Genuine separate planes: Y, Cb and Cr each in their own strips (6 strips total), with all four YCbCr tags. |
251: | `ycbcr-planar-2x2.tif` | PlanarConfig = 2, separate planes on a 2x2 base | conversion | Genuine separate planes: Y, Cb and Cr each in their own strips (3 strips total), with consistent strip arrays and all four YCbCr tags. |
252: | `ycbcr-tiled-2x2.tif` | 16x16 tiles, 4x3 grid (12 tiles) | tag-reading | Tile tag path together with all four YCbCr tags. |
253: 
254: libtiff's RGBA helper (`tiff2rgba`) cannot decode planar + subsampled YCbCr,
255: so the ground-truth PPM for `ycbcr-planar-2x2.tif` is rendered from the
256: equivalent chunky 2x2 YCbCr TIFF through the same `tiff2rgba` + `tifftopnm`
257: pipeline used for the other fixtures.
258: 
259: `ycbcr-tiled-2x2.tif` is a special case: `tiffcp` cannot tile subsampled input,
260: so the image was tiled while still 1x1 and the `YCbCrSubsampling` tag was set to
261: `2 2` afterwards. Its pixel data is therefore not subsampled; the fixture
262: exercises tag reading and tile traversal only.
263: 
264: ### Odd-dimension fixtures
265: 
266: Three images whose width and height are not multiples of the subsampling
267: factors, so the chroma dimensions use the ceiling rule. Tags and pixel data
268: agree, so all three are conversion tests.
269: 
270: | Test image | Dimensions | Subsampling | Kind | Validates |
271: |---|---|---|---|---|
272: | `ycbcr-odd-2x2.tif` | 61x47 | 2x2 | conversion | Ceiling of odd luma dimensions for 2x2 chroma. |
273: | `ycbcr-odd-4x4.tif` | 63x61 | 4x4 | conversion | Ceiling of odd luma dimensions for 4x4 chroma. |
274: | `ycbcr-odd-mixed.tif` | 62x47 | 2x1 | conversion | Ceiling on one axis only for mixed subsampling. |
275: 
276: ## Ground-truth reference images
277: 
278: `tests/reference_images/ycbcr-*.ppm` holds the RGB ground-truth images
279: corresponding to the 18 YCbCr test images, in binary Netpbm PPM (P6) format.
280: Each is produced with `tiff2rgba` followed by `tifftopnm`, and each P6 header
281: matches the dimensions of its TIFF (64x48, or the odd dimensions 61x47, 63x61
282: and 62x47). libtiff's YCbCr RGBA reader cannot decode 1x4 and 2x4 subsampling,
283: so those two references are rendered from the matching RGB source TIFF through
284: the same `tiff2rgba` + `tifftopnm` pipeline.

It's a robustness issue in `ReferenceBlackWhite::map()` (`include/tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp:233-237`):

```cpp
return (value - v[0]) * range / (v[1] - v[0]);
```

`v[0]`/`v[1]` are the reference black/white values for one component, read from TIFF tag 532 (or defaults). The constructor body is empty — unlike `YCbCrCoefficients` and `YCbCrSubSampling`, it validates nothing.

Two bad cases:

- **black == white** → division by zero. Since these are `float`s, you get `NaN` (when `value == black`) or `±inf`. The result is immediately assigned to `int32_t` in `convertYCbCrToRgb_` (`const int32_t y = refBlackWhite.map<0, 255.0f>(i8);`). Floating-point→integer conversion of NaN/inf is undefined behavior in C++; in practice you get `INT_MIN` or other garbage. `toFixed()`/`fromFixed()` then clamp the final pixel to 0–255, so it's not a memory-safety bug, but the output is meaningless.
- **black > white** → inverted scaling; no crash, just wrong range.

A malformed file can trigger this legitimately: tag 532 is RATIONAL, `copy<float>()` already rejects zero denominators, but a numerator/denominator pair like `128/1` for both black and white is perfectly parseable.

None of the 18 YCbCr fixtures hit it (defaults are 0/255 and 128/255; the headroom fixture is 15/235 and 128/240), so it isn't a blocker for #45. The natural fix is to validate in the constructor — throw `std::invalid_argument` when `v[2*i] >= v[2*i+1]` — which would match the validation style of the neighboring tag classes and protect every caller. The project defines an `INTERFACE` library target (`TiffCraft`) with include directories, but it did not install or export the CMake target itself. The root `CMakeLists.txt` unconditionally added tests, apps, and examples, which broke consumption as a dependency.

This PR adds:

1. **Namespaced alias target.** `add_library(TiffCraft::TiffCraft ALIAS TiffCraft)` so consumers can use `target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE TiffCraft::TiffCraft)`.

3. **`install()` and `install(EXPORT ...)` support.** `install(TARGETS TiffCraft EXPORT TiffCraftTargets)` + `install(EXPORT TiffCraftTargets NAMESPACE TiffCraft:: ...)`, plus generated `TiffCraftConfig.cmake`/`TiffCraftConfigVersion.cmake`, so `find_package(TiffCraft)` exposes `TiffCraft::TiffCraft`.
4. **FetchContent compatibility.** `FetchContent_MakeAvailable(TiffCraft)` + namespaced alias link.
5. **Versioned export.** `TiffCraftConfigVersion.cmake` generated from `PROJECT_VERSION` via `write_basic_package_version_file` (SameMajorVersion).
6. **Document consumption in the README.** FetchContent and `find_package` sections added.
7. **Automated consumer tests** under `tests/cmake-consumers/` covering the three consumption paths (FetchContent, find_package, subdirectory), plus a dedicated Linux CI job (`Ubuntu-Consumers`) that runs them.
